memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Your children who follow you in later generations and foreigners who come from distant lands will see the calamities that have fallen on the land and the diseases with which the Lord has afflicted it. The whole land will be a burning waste of salt and sulfur — nothing planted, nothing sprouting, no vegetation growing on it." — Deut 29:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses paints a stark picture of what covenant judgment would look like — a land turned into a burning waste of salt and sulfur, barren and lifeless, where nothing grows. He even echoes the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. Future generations and travellers from distant lands would look on the ruined land and be stunned. The devastation itself would become a lasting testimony.

There is something arresting about the idea that a ruined land could preach a sermon. The barrenness would silently declare a message to all who saw it: this is what it looks like when a people abandon the living God. Sin's consequences become visible, a warning written into the landscape itself.

We do not read this as a threat over believers today. But the underlying truth endures: turning from God, the source of all life, leads to barrenness. A life, a family, or a community cut off from God cannot flourish any more than a salted field can grow crops. Apart from Him, we wither.

The good news is that God specialises in reversing barrenness. He is the God who makes deserts bloom and brings life from death. Through Christ, the barren heart can become a fruitful garden, watered by His Spirit (John 7:38). Where sin brings a wasteland, Jesus brings living water. If your soul feels dry and barren today, come to Him. He can make what was desolate flourish again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I recognise that life apart from God leads to barrenness?
2. Where do I need God to bring life to a "barren" area of my heart?
3. How does Christ's promise of living water give me hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, apart from You I wither, but with You even the barren places can bloom. Where my soul feels dry, pour out Your living water and bring life again through Christ. Amen.
